feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Musician Sara Bareilles talks about the importance of crying in her life
entry.summary: On Wild Card, famous guests answer questions that we don't always talk about. Musician Sara Bareilles talks about the importance of crying in her life.

entry.title: A stranger helped a mother and son stuck in a current in Lake Michigan
entry.summary: A mother was caught in a current while saving her son in Lake Michigan. When she couldn't get them closer to shore, a man appeared to help.

entry.title: New book traces the pieces of steel salvaged from the World Trade Center
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Sam Holleran, one of the authors behind the new book Scattered Steel: the afterlife of the World Trade Center.

entry.title: At Minnesota's state fair, crop artists depict the struggle over immigration enforcement
entry.summary: Nearly 600 artists submitted crop art at the Minnesota State Fair. Using seeds from Minnesota grown crops, many artists created scenes inspired by Operation Metro Surge.

entry.title: This week in science: Archaeology fakes, hurricanes and lizards, and heat health effects
entry.summary: NPR's Regina Barber and Nate Rott talk about a new way to spot archaeological fakes, how hurricanes may have influenced lizard evolution and the health effects of extreme heat.

entry.title: Do you hate being middle-aged? NPR's Alllison Aubrey wants to change that
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Allison Aubrey, health and science correspondent for NPR and the author of Your Turn: How to Create a Midlife You Love. You can share your story of midlife reinvention.

entry.title: 'The health system in Nepal is not prepared for this'
entry.summary: That's the grim assessment from the ground in the wake of the catastrophic flooding, which damaged or destroyed 7 health facilities, interrupted routine care and is affecting mental health.

entry.title: El-Sayed split Michigan Democrats. Whether they unify could decide Senate control
entry.summary: After a bruising Senate primary, Michigan Democrats are trying to unify to hold onto a must-win seat. But healing those fissures is proving not so simple.

entry.title: Dolly Parton's music rises on the charts
entry.summary: The late country singer's hits are making a mark on the pop charts following her death. Many are charting higher than they ever have before — and the rise of country music might play a role.

entry.title: Kyiv's new reality: Russian drones by night — and now by day
entry.summary: More than a week of strikes by jet-powered Russian drones has disrupted schools, work and transport … and left Ukraine, which lacks air defense supplies, feeling vulnerable.
